title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 1
paragraphs: Meanwhile those of the Persians who had been left behind in Europe by Darius, under the command of Megabazus, had subdued first the people of Perinthus among the Hellespontians, since they refused to be subjects of Darius. These had in earlier days also been roughly handled by the Paeonians; for the Paeonians from the Strymon had been ordered by an oracle of their god to march against the Perinthians—and if, when encamped opposite them, the Perinthians should shout aloud and call to them by name, they were to attack; but if they did not shout to them, they were not to attack. This is what the Paeonians set out to do. When the Perinthians were encamped opposite them in the suburb of their city, a challenge was made and a single combat took place in three forms: man against man, horse against horse, and dog against dog. Then, as the Perinthians were getting the better of two of the three contests, in their exultation they raised the shout of paion; and the Paeonians guessed that this was the very thing the oracle had spoken of, and said to one another, “Surely the oracle is being fulfilled for us; now it is time to act.” So the Paeonians attacked the Perinthians when they had raised the shout of paion, and much the better of the fight, and left only a few of them alive.
